answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to carry a lantern credential: a signed, public record of its past work, staked with a refundable deposit and countersigned by two established peers. Each action is sealed with the agent's quill, its private key, so fake identities cannot borrow another's history. An agent that tries to wander in under a fresh name starts with no lantern and no stake, and must complete small, paid, verifiable jobs before it can touch anything valuable — creating a hundred sock puppets then costs a hundred deposits and a hundred slow reputations.
